messages.subject: reduced mixed effects model fails to converge
messages.subject_clean: reduced mixed effects model fails to converge
messages.body_plain:
Hello list,

We are currently analyzing data for a speech perception study in which we
are trying to determine whether a condition with two levels has an effect
on recognition accuracy (coded as 0 or 1). Condition was manipulated within
subjects, and all items appeared in all conditions. The full model with the
maximal random effects structure failed to converge, so we removed random
effects based on contributions to total variance until we reached the
maximal model that would converge:

 model_full <- glmer(RESP ~ condition + (1 + condition | item) + (1 |
participant), data = data, family = binomial)

Since we are interested in the effect of condition, we want to perform a
likelihood ratio test comparing the full model to a reduced model that
lacks condition as a fixed effect, but is identical in all other respects.

model_reduced <- glmer(RESP ~ (1 + condition | item) + (1 | participant),
data = data, family = binomial)

However, this reduced model fails to converge. We are getting the following
warning message when we attempt to build the reduced model:
[image: Inline image 1]

When we view the summary output for the reduced model (to examine
contributions to total variance), it appears that the model was
successfully built (“PID” = participant ID #; “Stim” = stimulus item).
[image: Inline image 2]

We have several questions. Can we proceed with comparing the models despite
the warning message? Why is it that the full model converged but the
reduced model failed to converge? Might it have to do with the fact that
the reduced model has no fixed effects, only random effects? Because
“condition” in this example has only two levels, we could simply examine
the summary output for the full model to determine the significance of the
variable, but we have other data in which the variable of interest has more
levels, and we anticipate this problem arising in the future.

Thanks in advance!
Best,
Julia

--
Julia Strand, PhD
Assistant Professor of Psychology
Carleton College
One North College Street
Northfield, MN 55057
507-222-5637
Website <https://apps.carleton.edu/curricular/psyc/jstrand/>

messages.subject: Re: reduced mixed effects model fails to converge
messages.subject_clean: reduced mixed effects model fails to converge
messages.body_plain:
Dear Julia,

You might find that changing the optimizer helps you achieve convergence.
The command would be

 model_full <- glmer(RESP ~ condition + (1 + condition | item) + (1 |
participant), data = data, family = binomial, control=glmerControl(optimizer
="bobyqa"))


[also insert this in the subset model]

When you get a convergence failure, the model fitting algorithm is telling
you that the solution it found is not likely to be the best solution. You
can still inspect the (bad) solution it found, but it's not clear if you
should rely on it.

You might also want to assess whether the full model that did converge is
overparameterized; Bates and colleagues have outlined one such procedure:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.04967.pdf

If none of these solutions help, there's two basic ways forward (both of
which are anticonservative):

   1. Simplify the full model by removing (condition random slopes,
   correlations) until the subset model converges.
   2. Do not use the likelihood ratio test to test for effects; use Wald Z
   here.

Hope that helps!

Matt
